subject: Litmus POC alignment & initial prompt suite plan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@litmus.ai>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya@litmus.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & proposed POC scope (next steps)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we can get a small pilot underway with clear success measures.

Key pains you highlighted:
- Incoming support docs and release notes are unstructured; agents spend ~30–40% of time searching and re-phrasing content to answer tickets.
- Latency and cost with current embedding+search setup at scale; searches spike during releases.
- Regulatory need to keep PII out of hosted logs for certain cohorts.

Pilot goals (30 days):
1) Reduce average time-to-first-draft answer by 25% on triage tickets (priority criteria).
2) Demonstrate sub-150ms median gen latency for 512-token prompts under steady-state load for the support assistant route.
3) Validate prompt/eval set with a >=0.75 helpfulness score (internal rubric).

Proposed scope and deliverables:
- Environment: Redwood hosted sandbox tied to Litmus dev workspace (non-prod).
- Model stack: rdx-small-v2 for rapid iterate, with a quantized variant for cost checks.
- Prompt/eval: we’ll run the 40-scenario prompt suite we sketched on the call; you’ll supply 20 canonical tickets and we’ll seed 20 synthetic edge cases.
- Owners: Litmus — Priya (product) for ticket selection; Redwood — Jordan (sales) + Irene (onboarding lead) for ops/telemetry.
- Access: you’ll grant a dev service account with read-only storage access; we’ll provide an access checklist.

Immediate asks / timeline:
- Please confirm the 20-ticket sample by EOD Mon (Mar 27).
- Approve the mutual action plan PDF I attached and confirm a preferred kickoff window week of Apr 1.
- Security: please share your SOC2 questions; Irene will follow up with the evidence map.

Attachments: MAP_Litmus_Redwood_v1.pdf (mutual action plan), litmus-access-checklist.csv

If that aligns, I’ll book a 30-min kickoff with the technical owner and Ops.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex@litmus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya@litmus.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 17:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & proposed POC scope (next steps)

Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. This matches our notes. A few clarifications: 

1) Ticket sample: we’ll extract 20 recent support tickets (redacted) by end of day Monday — Priya will own.
2) Latency target: 150ms median sounds good, but can you confirm the load profile you’ll use for steady-state? We expect ~30 qps for the assistant route during peak.
3) Security: we need confirmation that Redwood’s hosted sandbox logs can be disabled for our test tenant and that keys are customer-managed for the pilot.

Once we have the MAP, we’ll get legal to look. Assuming all good, Apr 2 or Apr 3 kickoff would work for our side.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Product
Litmus AI

Alex — great, thanks for the confirmations. Answering your questions inline and adding ops detail so we can close the kickoff date: 

- Load profile: we’ll validate at 30 QPS steady-state (50 RPS short bursts for release windows); test harness will replay production-shaped traces you provide.
- Logs: we can disable request/response logging for the Litmus sandbox and we support customer-managed keys (via your KMS) for the pilot keys. Irene will send the evidence map and a short diagram of what is logged by default.

Proposed immediate schedule:
- Mon, Mar 27: Litmus delivers 20-ticket sample + NDA comments (if any).
- Tue, Mar 28: Redwood ingests sample; baseline eval run and short findings doc.
- Wed, Mar 29: Joint prompt calibration session (30 min).
- Tue, Apr 2: Formal kickoff (30 min) — demo access, rollout plan, and telemetry checks.

Ben / Irene — looping you in to confirm the test harness support and to request the SOC2 evidence handoff. Ben, can you confirm who on CS/Platform will own the 30 QPS test and whether we need a dedicated Dedicated pool for the spike?

Attached the MAP and access checklist again.

Best — Jordan
--
